title: Nagano vs Hakone: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Nagano for depth, authenticity, snow monkeys, and value. Hakone for a quick, easy Tokyo escape with Mt. Fuji views and luxury ryokans.

categories.name: Onsen & Hot Springs
categories.summary: Shibu Onsen's 9 historic public baths and retro ryokan village beats Hakone's commoditized private-rotenburo hotels on authentic experience.

categories.name: Temples & Culture
categories.summary: Zenkoji Temple (1,400 years old), Matsumoto Castle, and Togakushi Shrine give Nagano overwhelming cultural depth.

categories.name: Nature & Scenery
categories.summary: Hakone wins on dramatic volcanic scenery and Fuji views (weather permitting). Nagano wins for authentic alpine wilderness and snow monkeys.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: Nagano ryokans ¥12,000–25,000/night vs Hakone ¥20,000–50,000+. Daily budget also cheaper in Nagano.

categories.name: Transit from Tokyo
categories.summary: Hakone Free Pass covers everything for ¥6,000. Nagano snow monkey trip involves 3 transit legs and infrequent buses.

categories.name: Crowds
categories.summary: Hakone is heavily over-touristed, especially weekends. Nagano is quieter and more authentic.

categories.name: Skiing
categories.summary: Nagano hosted 1998 Olympics. Multiple world-class resorts nearby. Hakone has no skiing.

faq.question: Is Nagano or Hakone better for a day trip from Tokyo?
faq.answer: Hakone — 80–90 min one-way vs Nagano's 2.5+ hour multi-leg journey to the snow monkeys.

faq.question: When are the snow monkeys in the hot springs?
faq.answer: Peak season is November through March when temperatures are below freezing.

faq.question: Which is cheaper, Nagano or Hakone?
faq.answer: Nagano — ryokans are 30–50% cheaper, and daily costs are lower throughout.
